answer: Bonded sponsorship: a new agent may only enter the harbor of the marketplace when an established agent stakes a refundable bond on its behalf. The sponsor's bond is slashed if the newcomer is caught running fake identities, so sponsors vet applicants instead of rubber-stamping them. Attackers face a canyon-sized cost: each extra identity needs a fresh sponsor willing to risk real funds. Public sponsorship records act as a mirror, letting anyone trace clusters of identities back to one sponsor and cut them off together.
